title: How Long After Hardwood Installation Can You Walk on It and Move Furniture?
meta: Nail-down prefinished hardwood: walk on it the same day. Glue-down: 24 hours to walk, 48 to 72 for furniture. Site-finished: 3 days. Wills Flooring, Kirkland.
keywords: how long after hardwood installation can you walk on it, when can I move furniture on new hardwood floors, glue down hardwood cure time, new hardwood floor wait time, hardwood installation Kirkland WA
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: It depends on how the floor was attached. Nail-down and floating prefinished hardwood can be walked on the same day and furnished that evening. Glue-down needs 24 hours before foot traffic and 48 to 72 hours before heavy furniture. Site-finished floors follow the finish, not the install: 24 hours for socks, 72 for furniture, 7 days for rugs.
blocks.detail: Those are the timelines we give every Kirkland customer at the walkthrough. The install method is decided at the estimate, so you will know your wait before the first box is opened.

blocks.html: The question usually arrives by text on the last day of the job: the crew is packing up, the couch is in the garage, and the family wants to know whether tonight is fine. Most of the confusion online comes from mixing up two different waits. One is the adhesive or fastener holding the boards down. The other is the finish on top. Prefinished hardwood, which is most of what we install in Kirkland, has a factory-cured finish, so only the fastening matters. Site-finished floors have wet finish on them and follow the refinishing clock instead.

blocks.note: Times assume a normal Kirkland interior at 60 to 75°F with the heat running. Cold rooms slow every adhesive and every finish.

blocks.text: Why glue-down is the one that makes you wait

items.title: Adhesive cures, it does not dry
items.text: Modern urethane and silane hardwood adhesives cure by reacting with moisture in the air and the subfloor. They skin over in an hour and hold the plank in place, but full bond strength takes 48 to 72 hours. Walking gently on day two is fine. Dragging a loaded dresser is not.

items.title: Where Kirkland floors get glued
items.text: Glue-down is our default over concrete: Houghton and Juanita condos, walk-out basements in Finn Hill, slab additions in Rose Hill. It is also the quietest method over a family room, so some Bridle Trails owners ask for it on plywood too.

items.title: Temperature is the hidden variable
items.text: A slab that sits at 55°F in February cures adhesive slowly. We ask you to run the heat for 48 hours before we start and keep it on for three days after, and we will not glue a floor to a slab that fails a moisture test.

items.title: The hollow-spot problem
items.text: If a heavy leg lands on a plank before the adhesive sets, it presses the plank into the trowel ridges and squeezes glue sideways. The plank stays down but taps hollow. That is why the 72-hour furniture rule exists.

blocks.text: Price your Kirkland hardwood installation right now

blocks.note: Glue-down over concrete needs a moisture test and sometimes a sealer, both quoted at the free estimate.

blocks.text: Moving furniture back in the right order

items.text: Before anything comes in, walk every room in socks. Listen for clicks or hollow taps. On a floating floor, check that transitions are seated. Anything odd is easier to fix with the room empty, and it is covered by our 1-year workmanship warranty.

Felt pads on all chair, table and sofa feet, and hard plastic or felt glides on anything with a wheel. New prefinished floors have a tough aluminum oxide finish, but a bare metal leg dragged across it still scratches.
items.note: Pads first, furniture second. Not the other way around.

items.text: Two people per heavy piece, lifted and set down. If a piece must slide, put a clean moving blanket or a piece of the leftover cardboard underneath. This is the rule that matters most on a fresh glue-down.
Rugs can go down the same day on prefinished floors. On a site-finished floor, wait 7 days so the finish can off-gas and harden evenly. Fridges go back on a hardboard runner, never rolled directly.

blocks.text: Site-finished floors: a different clock entirely

blocks.html: If you chose unfinished hardwood so the boards could be sanded flat and stained to match an existing floor, the install itself is done on day one or two. What follows is the same sanding, sealing and three coats of water-based finish we use on a refinish, and the same waiting periods. We covered those hour by hour in our post on walking on refinished floors. The short version: socks after 24 hours, shoes and light furniture after 48, heavy furniture after 72, rugs after a week, full hardness at about 30 days.

blocks.title: One Kirkland-specific note:
blocks.text: Lakefront and view homes in Houghton and Juanita often have large south and west windows. Direct sun on a fresh water-based finish is fine, but sun on a curing glue-down floor with the windows shut can drive the surface past 90°F and flash the adhesive at the edges. Crack a window or run the AC for the first three days.
Mistakes we get called back for

items.html: Rolling the fridge straight across a glue-down on day one. Four small wheels carrying 300 pounds is exactly the point load a curing adhesive cannot handle. Use a hardboard path and wait three days.
Taping plastic over the floor to protect it. Tape can pull factory finish, and plastic traps moisture over a curing glue-down. Use rosin paper and tape it to itself.
Turning the heat off while the house is empty. A cold, damp Kirkland February room slows adhesive cure and leaves the boards adjusting for weeks.
Screwing a bed frame or island through a floating floor. A floating floor has to move as a sheet. Pinning it creates gaps at the far wall by next winter.

items: Ask the crew chief which method was used in each room; mixed-method jobs are common in split-level Kirkland homes.
Get the wait for foot traffic and for furniture in writing on the walkthrough sheet.
Keep the heat between 60 and 75°F and humidity between 35 and 55 percent for the first week.
Buy felt pads and glides before install day, not after.
Plan a hardboard runner for the refrigerator and the piano.
Tap-test a glue-down floor before furniture goes back, and call (425) 350-4435 if anything sounds hollow.

faq.q: Can I walk on new hardwood floors the same day they are installed?
faq.a: Yes for nail-down and floating prefinished floors, which are most Kirkland installs. The boards are held mechanically and the finish came cured from the factory. Glue-down floors want 24 hours before regular walking, and site-finished floors want 24 hours after the last coat of finish before socks-only traffic.

faq.q: How long should I wait to move heavy furniture onto glue-down hardwood?
faq.a: Wait 48 to 72 hours. The adhesive holds the plank within an hour but reaches full bond strength over about three days. Heavy point loads before then can press a plank into the glue ridges and leave a hollow-sounding spot that is annoying to fix later.

faq.q: When can I put rugs on a new hardwood floor?
faq.a: Same day on prefinished hardwood. On a site-finished floor, wait 7 days so the finish can cure evenly and the rug does not leave a sheen difference. Use rug pads that are labeled safe for hardwood finishes, since some rubber pads can discolor the surface over time.

faq.q: Do I need to keep the heat on after hardwood is installed in winter?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the house between 60 and 75°F for at least a week. Cold rooms slow glue-down adhesive and site-applied finishes, and a big temperature swing right after install can open small gaps between boards. Normal Kirkland thermostat settings are fine; just do not turn it off.

faq.q: How long does a full hardwood installation take before the waiting even starts?
faq.a: Most 800 to 1,200 sq ft prefinished jobs take two to three working days including tear-out and trim. Glue-down adds prep time for moisture testing and sometimes a sealer. Unfinished floors add three to four days of sanding and finishing on top of the install.

faq.q: Can my dog walk on the new floor right away?
faq.a: On prefinished nail-down or floating floors, yes, the same day. On glue-down, treat the dog like light foot traffic and keep it off for 24 hours. On site-finished floors, keep pets out for at least 48 hours since claws mark a finish that has not hardened.
